statement.title: B. Array Craft
statement.input_spec:
The first line contains an integer $t$ ($1 \leq t \leq 10^4$) — the number of test cases.

For each test case:

 The only line contains three integers $n$, $x$, and $y$ ($2 \leq n \leq 10^5, 1 \le y \lt x \le n)$.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $n$ over all test cases will not exceed $10^5$.
statement.output_spec: For each test case, output $n$ space-separated integers $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ in a new line.
statement.note:
In the second test case,

 $i=x=4$ is the smallest index that satisfies $a_1+\ldots +a_i=\max_{j=1}^{n}(a_1+\ldots+a_j)=2$;

 $i=y=3$ is the greatest index that satisfies $a_i+\ldots +a_n=\max_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+\ldots+a_n)=2$.

Thus, the array $a=[1,-1,1,1]$ is considered correct.

editorial.tutorial:
B — Array Craft

hint1

Starting from a trival construction.

hint2

Utilize the condition $x \gt y$.

solution

First, we consider making $presum_x \gt presum_j$ for all $x \lt i \le n$, and similarly for $y$. We can think of a trivial construction: $a[r, \ldots ,l]=[1, \ldots ,1], a[1, \ldots...,r-1]=[-1, \ldots, -1]$ and $a[l+1,\ldots,n]=[-1, \ldots, -1]$.

The construction doesn't works when $presum_x \lt 0$, but we are close to the correct solution. Next, we will make a little adjustment: $a[r, \ldots, l]=[1,\ldots,1], a[1, \ldots...,r-1]=[\ldots,1, -1]$ and $a[l+1,\ldots,n]=[-1,1, \ldots]$.

It is not hard to see $presum_x \ge presum_j$ for all $x \lt i \le n$, and for $1 \le i \le y$, $\max(presum_i)-min(presum_i)\le 1$. Thus, we get $presum_x \ge 2+presum_{y-1} \ge 2+min(presum_i) \ge 1+max(presum_i)$. The same applies to the suffix sum as well. Therefore, this construction is valid.

Time complexity: $O(n)$.

Bonus

Solve the problem when $x \le y$.
